title: Longest Special Path
summary: Given an undirected tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where edges are defined by a 2D array, and an array of node values, find the longest path where all node values are unique, and the minimum number of nodes in such paths.
statement: Given an undirected tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where edges are defined by a 2D array, and an array of node values, find the longest path where all node values are unique, and the minimum number of nodes in such paths. The result is returned as an array of two elements: the path length and the minimum number of nodes.
constraints: edges describes a rooted-at-zero weighted tree with up to 50,000 nodes and positive weights.
A special path travels downward from an ancestor to a descendant and contains unique node values.
Return [maximum edge-length sum, minimum node count among paths with that length].
hints: Along one root-to-node path, the valid ancestor range is a sliding window of unique values.
Track each value’s latest depth and prefix distance while depth-first traversal backtracks state.
Advance the left depth past repeats; measure distance to the current node and restore last positions on exit.
The window is the longest unique suffix ending at each node, and every downward ancestor path appears as such a suffix candidate.
editorial: The window is the longest unique suffix ending at each node, and every downward ancestor path appears as such a suffix candidate.

tests.explanation: The best unique downward path has weight six and, among ties, two nodes.
Repeated values prevent using both nodes; the best length is zero with one node.
